newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended lower in slow trade. The spot September contract was the only winner, ending $6.00 up at $1,583 while November shed $13.00 to end at $1,482. In New York arabica futures ended near unchanged after yet another bid to push through resistance was countered by persistent producer-related selling. Traders continued to monitor events in Colombia, where the unstable political situation could affect production and exports. On Friday leftist rebels reportedly set five busses ablaze in the central coffee-growing province of Tolima.

ACPC - The Association of Coffee Producing Countries will discuss how effective last year's export plan was and how well the current plan is progressing at its next meeting, scheduled for September 27 and 28. The technical group which comprises Brazil, Colombia, El Salvador, Ivory Coast, Uganda and Indonesia will assess how well the 1995/96 (July/June) export retention scheme was implemented and what the situation is in July/June 1996/97. According to preliminary figures ACPC members exported 47 million bags in July/June 1995/96, 3 per cent above the original target of 45.8 million bags. Both Guatemala and Mexico are not attending the meeting and said they are not interested in joining the ACPC retention scheme.

BELGIUM- Belgium imported 176,046 bags of coffee in April 1996, 2.5 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 641,200 bags, 7.7 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.5 per cent to 2.068 million bags. The main supplier of green coffee in January/April 1996 was Brazil with 54,600 bags, down from 71,200 bags shipped the same four months the previous year. Exports in January/April 1996 totalled 452,200 bags, 13 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped slightly by 7 per cent to 1.204 million bags.

POLAND - Poland imported 667,100 bags of coffee in January/May 1996, 1.7 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose by 6.5 per cent to 1.536 million bags, up from 1.442 million bags the previous year. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/May 1996 were Ivory Coast (69,700 vs 99,100 bags), India (80,700 vs 34,100 bags), Indonesia (122,700 vs 87,000 bags) and Vietnam (114,200 vs 129,900 bags). The country exported 31,200 bags of coffee in January/May 1996 which compares to 17,100 bags the same months in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 reached 42,300 bags, up from 17,000 bags in 1994.
